### 50.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-50-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-50-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-50-D01
**Title:** Context Assembly Pipeline
**Purpose:** context budgets, source hierarchy, truncation, compression, and integrity
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-50-D03 — State diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-50-D03
**Title:** Context Assembly Pipeline
**Purpose:** context budgets, source hierarchy, truncation, compression, and integrity
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Registered
  Registered --> Ready: contract and policy validated
  Ready --> Running: authorized invocation
  Running --> Waiting: dependency or approval
  Waiting --> Running: condition satisfied

  Running --> Failed: terminal failure
  Failed --> Recovered: replay, compensate, or operator repair
  Recovered --> Ready
  Succeeded --> [*]
```

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

## 51. Prompt Assembly Architecture

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-51
**Decision status:** Part 3 implementation blueprint; provider-specific choices require an accepted technology decision.

### Scope and architectural intent

This subsystem governs templates, instructions, variables, policies, examples, and versioning. It is a capability boundary, not a license to bypass the domain owner. A human reader must be able to identify the source of truth, the permitted autonomy, and the recovery path. An AI coding agent must be able to identify the exact interfaces it may change and the tests required before it proposes a patch.

### 51.1 Architecture Decision Record

The subsystem MUST make this concern explicit, typed, observable, attributable, and reviewable. It MUST fail closed when required evidence is missing.

**Decision application:** Templates, instructions, variables, policies, examples, and versioning is implemented behind an owned port, with policy inside and providers outside. The contract is versioned and linked to tests, telemetry, runbooks, and the section ADR.

### 51.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-51-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-51-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-51-D01
**Title:** Prompt Assembly Architecture
**Purpose:** templates, instructions, variables, policies, examples, and versioning
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

## 52. Tool Calling Architecture

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-52
**Decision status:** Part 3 implementation blueprint; provider-specific choices require an accepted technology decision.

### Scope and architectural intent

This subsystem governs tool registration, schemas, authorization, invocation, and receipts. It is a capability boundary, not a license to bypass the domain owner. A human reader must be able to identify the source of truth, the permitted autonomy, and the recovery path. An AI coding agent must be able to identify the exact interfaces it may change and the tests required before it proposes a patch.

### 52.1 Architecture Decision Record

The subsystem MUST make this concern explicit, typed, observable, attributable, and reviewable. It MUST fail closed when required evidence is missing.

**Decision application:** Tool registration, schemas, authorization, invocation, and receipts is implemented behind an owned port, with policy inside and providers outside. The contract is versioned and linked to tests, telemetry, runbooks, and the section ADR.

### 53.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-53-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-53-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-53-D01
**Title:** Reasoning Pipeline
**Purpose:** evidence, hypotheses, inference, uncertainty, verification, and explanation
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-53-D02 — Sequence diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-53-D02
**Title:** Reasoning Pipeline
**Purpose:** evidence, hypotheses, inference, uncertainty, verification, and explanation
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as AI caller

  A->>C: request scoped context

  R-->>A: receipt, evidence, and next state
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-53-D03 — State diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-53-D03
**Title:** Reasoning Pipeline
**Purpose:** evidence, hypotheses, inference, uncertainty, verification, and explanation
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Registered
  Registered --> Ready: contract and policy validated
  Ready --> Running: authorized invocation
  Running --> Waiting: dependency or approval
  Waiting --> Running: condition satisfied
  Running --> Succeeded: verified postcondition
  Running --> Failed: terminal failure
  Failed --> Recovered: replay, compensate, or operator repair
  Recovered --> Ready
  Succeeded --> [*]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
```

### 54.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-54-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-54-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-54-D01
**Title:** Planning Pipeline
**Purpose:** goals, decomposition, constraints, plan validation, and replanning
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-54-D03 — State diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-54-D03
**Title:** Planning Pipeline

**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Registered
  Registered --> Ready: contract and policy validated
  Ready --> Running: authorized invocation
  Running --> Waiting: dependency or approval

  Running --> Failed: terminal failure

  Recovered --> Ready
  Succeeded --> [*]
```

```text
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

## 55. Execution Pipeline

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-55
**Decision status:** Part 3 implementation blueprint; provider-specific choices require an accepted technology decision.

### Scope and architectural intent

This subsystem governs approved steps, effects, checkpoints, compensation, and completion. It is a capability boundary, not a license to bypass the domain owner. A human reader must be able to identify the source of truth, the permitted autonomy, and the recovery path. An AI coding agent must be able to identify the exact interfaces it may change and the tests required before it proposes a patch.

### 55.1 Architecture Decision Record

The subsystem MUST make this concern explicit, typed, observable, attributable, and reviewable. It MUST fail closed when required evidence is missing.

**Decision application:** Approved steps, effects, checkpoints, compensation, and completion is implemented behind an owned port, with policy inside and providers outside. The contract is versioned and linked to tests, telemetry, runbooks, and the section ADR.

### 55.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-55-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-55-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-55-D01
**Title:** Execution Pipeline
**Purpose:** approved steps, effects, checkpoints, compensation, and completion
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-55-D03 — State diagram

## 56. Reflection Pipeline

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-56
**Decision status:** Part 3 implementation blueprint; provider-specific choices require an accepted technology decision.

### Scope and architectural intent

This subsystem governs self-checks, critique, evaluator separation, and bounded revision. It is a capability boundary, not a license to bypass the domain owner. A human reader must be able to identify the source of truth, the permitted autonomy, and the recovery path. An AI coding agent must be able to identify the exact interfaces it may change and the tests required before it proposes a patch.

### 56.1 Architecture Decision Record

The subsystem MUST make this concern explicit, typed, observable, attributable, and reviewable. It MUST fail closed when required evidence is missing.

**Decision application:** Self-checks, critique, evaluator separation, and bounded revision is implemented behind an owned port, with policy inside and providers outside. The contract is versioned and linked to tests, telemetry, runbooks, and the section ADR.

### 57.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-57-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-57-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-57-D01
**Title:** Learning Pipeline
**Purpose:** feedback ingestion, evaluation, updates, regressions, and promotion
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-57-D02 — Sequence diagram

**Title:** Learning Pipeline

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as AI caller
```

### CAT-ARCH-P3-57-D03 — State diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-57-D03
**Title:** Learning Pipeline
**Purpose:** feedback ingestion, evaluation, updates, regressions, and promotion
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Registered
  Registered --> Ready: contract and policy validated
  Ready --> Running: authorized invocation
  Running --> Waiting: dependency or approval
  Waiting --> Running: condition satisfied
  Running --> Succeeded: verified postcondition
  Running --> Failed: terminal failure
  Failed --> Recovered: replay, compensate, or operator repair
  Recovered --> Ready
  Succeeded --> [*]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

### 58.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-58-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-58-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-58-D01
**Title:** Feedback Architecture
**Purpose:** human feedback, telemetry, outcomes, labels, and governance
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

## 59. AI Safety Architecture

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-59
**Decision status:** Part 3 implementation blueprint; provider-specific choices require an accepted technology decision.

### Scope and architectural intent

This subsystem governs policy enforcement, sandboxing, red teaming, monitoring, and incident response. It is a capability boundary, not a license to bypass the domain owner. A human reader must be able to identify the source of truth, the permitted autonomy, and the recovery path. An AI coding agent must be able to identify the exact interfaces it may change and the tests required before it proposes a patch.

### 59.1 Architecture Decision Record

The subsystem MUST make this concern explicit, typed, observable, attributable, and reviewable. It MUST fail closed when required evidence is missing.

**Decision application:** Policy enforcement, sandboxing, red teaming, monitoring, and incident response is implemented behind an owned port, with policy inside and providers outside. The contract is versioned and linked to tests, telemetry, runbooks, and the section ADR.

### 59.24 Architecture decision record

**ADR:** CAT-ARCH-P3-59-ADR

- **Problem:** AI behavior can become opaque, over-privileged, provider-coupled, and difficult to recover.
- **Decision:** Keep intelligence behind governed runtime ports; separate proposal, policy, effect, evidence, and learning.
- **Rationale:** This preserves human control and makes AI behavior legible to humans and future models.
- **Rejected alternatives:** Direct model-to-database access, unrestricted tool lists, implicit memory authority, and unversioned prompt changes.
- **Consequences:** More metadata, evaluation, and control-plane work; safer evolution and lower incident ambiguity.
- **Review triggers:** New autonomy, new data class, new tool, new model provider, new tenant boundary, or changed SLO.

### CAT-ARCH-P3-59-D01 — Context diagram

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-59-D01
**Title:** AI Safety Architecture
**Purpose:** policy enforcement, sandboxing, red teaming, monitoring, and incident response
**Primary Audience:** Human architects, implementers, operators, and AI coding agents.
**Reading Order:** Identity and boundary first; then inputs, policy, runtime flow, effects, evidence, failure, and recovery.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Identity[Identity and tenant] --> Context[Context assembly]
  Context --> Agent[Agent policy]
  Agent --> Reason[Reasoning and plan]
  Reason --> Execute[Tool execution]
  Execute --> Evidence[Evidence and event]
  Evidence --> Memory[Scoped memory]
  Memory --> Context
  Agent -.->|must not bypass| Policy[Governance policy]
  Execute -.->|must not own| Domain[Domain authority]
```

ASCII architecture:

```text
[identity] -> [context] -> [policy] -> [reasoning] -> [approved effect]
                                  |                    |
                              [audit] <- [evidence] <- [result]
```

## 60. Architecture Part 3 Completion Contract

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-60
**Decision status:** Part 3 implementation blueprint; provider-specific choices require an accepted technology decision.

### Scope and architectural intent

This subsystem governs implementation evidence and consistency requirements for the AI architecture. It is a capability boundary, not a license to bypass the domain owner. A human reader must be able to identify the source of truth, the permitted autonomy, and the recovery path. An AI coding agent must be able to identify the exact interfaces it may change and the tests required before it proposes a patch.

### 60.1 Architecture Decision Record

The subsystem MUST make this concern explicit, typed, observable, attributable, and reviewable. It MUST fail closed when required evidence is missing.

**Decision application:** Implementation evidence and consistency requirements for the ai architecture is implemented behind an owned port, with policy inside and providers outside. The contract is versioned and linked to tests, telemetry, runbooks, and the section ADR.

## Part 3 cross-subsystem contracts

| Contract | Required property | Validation evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Agent identity | Stable identity, version, owner, capability set, and policy profile. | Registry and authorization test. |
| Context integrity | Ordered sources, provenance, classification, budget, and truncation record. | Context manifest and replay test. |
| Prompt integrity | Versioned template, variables, instructions, policy injection defense, and output schema. | Prompt snapshot and evaluation suite. |
| Tool safety | Typed schema, authorization, idempotency, deadline, receipt, and compensation. | Tool contract and fault tests. |
| Memory safety | Scope, consent, retention, deletion, provenance, and access decision. | Isolation and deletion tests. |
| Collaboration | Delegated task, bounded authority, correlation, deadline, and disagreement path. | Communication contract test. |
| Learning safety | Evaluation set, regression gate, approval, version, and rollback. | Promotion record and rollback drill. |
| Human control | Review threshold, escalation, interruption, and incident evidence. | Approval and kill-switch exercise. |

## Part 3 completion contract

Part 3 is complete when every section 41–60 has the mandatory decision and contract fields, each subsystem has all required input/output/interface/runtime fields, every diagram has Architecture ID, title, purpose, primary audience, and reading order, and the AI execution view is explicit for Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and future AI models. Runtime, security, memory, knowledge, context, communication, dependency, and recovery behavior must agree.

```text
python tools/validate_dependencies.py context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md
```

### P3-EVIDENCE-001 — Agent Identity

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-001
**Title:** Agent Identity implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one agent identity obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Related rules:** `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `.ai/RULES.md`, `.ai/AI_WORKFLOW.md`, and relevant security, coding, deployment, and directory rules.

**Related ADR:** `CAT-ARCH-P3-41-ADR`; create or update the ADR whenever authority, trust, data, autonomy, provider, SLO, or deployment changes.

**Related documents:** `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the owning context, contract definitions, and recovery runbooks.

**AI context window:** The context manifest MUST include source hierarchy, authoritative facts, invariants, allowed tools, policy profile, tenant, data classification, budget, deadline, output schema, and acceptance tests.

**Verification:** Unit, contract, architecture, dependency, runtime, communication, knowledge-flow, context-flow, security, duplicate, timeout, and recovery tests are required at the risk-appropriate level.

**Review questions:** What is authoritative? What is proposed? What crosses the trust boundary? Can it run twice? How is refusal represented? How does an operator stop it? What proves success?

**Non-compliance:** Stop implementation, record the missing evidence, assign an owner, and either add the control or approve a time-bounded exception with compensating controls.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Related rules:** `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `.ai/RULES.md`, `.ai/AI_WORKFLOW.md`, and relevant security, coding, deployment, and directory rules.

**Related ADR:** `CAT-ARCH-P3-48-ADR`; create or update the ADR whenever authority, trust, data, autonomy, provider, SLO, or deployment changes.

**Related documents:** `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the owning context, contract definitions, and recovery runbooks.

**AI context window:** The context manifest MUST include source hierarchy, authoritative facts, invariants, allowed tools, policy profile, tenant, data classification, budget, deadline, output schema, and acceptance tests.

**Verification:** Unit, contract, architecture, dependency, runtime, communication, knowledge-flow, context-flow, security, duplicate, timeout, and recovery tests are required at the risk-appropriate level.

**Review questions:** What is authoritative? What is proposed? What crosses the trust boundary? Can it run twice? How is refusal represented? How does an operator stop it? What proves success?

**Non-compliance:** Stop implementation, record the missing evidence, assign an owner, and either add the control or approve a time-bounded exception with compensating controls.

### P3-EVIDENCE-016 — Reflection

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-016
**Title:** Reflection implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one reflection obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

### P3-EVIDENCE-031 — Prompt Assembly

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-031
**Title:** Prompt Assembly implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one prompt assembly obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Purpose:** Make one multi-agent collaboration obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Related rules:** `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `.ai/RULES.md`, `.ai/AI_WORKFLOW.md`, and relevant security, coding, deployment, and directory rules.

**Related ADR:** `CAT-ARCH-P3-46-ADR`; create or update the ADR whenever authority, trust, data, autonomy, provider, SLO, or deployment changes.

**Related documents:** `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the owning context, contract definitions, and recovery runbooks.

**AI context window:** The context manifest MUST include source hierarchy, authoritative facts, invariants, allowed tools, policy profile, tenant, data classification, budget, deadline, output schema, and acceptance tests.

**Verification:** Unit, contract, architecture, dependency, runtime, communication, knowledge-flow, context-flow, security, duplicate, timeout, and recovery tests are required at the risk-appropriate level.

**Review questions:** What is authoritative? What is proposed? What crosses the trust boundary? Can it run twice? How is refusal represented? How does an operator stop it? What proves success?

**Non-compliance:** Stop implementation, record the missing evidence, assign an owner, and either add the control or approve a time-bounded exception with compensating controls.

### P3-EVIDENCE-054 — Planning

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-054
**Title:** Planning implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one planning obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

### P3-EVIDENCE-069 — Knowledge Retrieval

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-069
**Title:** Knowledge Retrieval implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one knowledge retrieval obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

### P3-EVIDENCE-084 — Agent Communication

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-084
**Title:** Agent Communication implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one agent communication obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Related rules:** `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `.ai/RULES.md`, `.ai/AI_WORKFLOW.md`, and relevant security, coding, deployment, and directory rules.

**Related ADR:** `CAT-ARCH-P3-44-ADR`; create or update the ADR whenever authority, trust, data, autonomy, provider, SLO, or deployment changes.

**Related documents:** `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the owning context, contract definitions, and recovery runbooks.

**AI context window:** The context manifest MUST include source hierarchy, authoritative facts, invariants, allowed tools, policy profile, tenant, data classification, budget, deadline, output schema, and acceptance tests.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Related rules:** `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `.ai/RULES.md`, `.ai/AI_WORKFLOW.md`, and relevant security, coding, deployment, and directory rules.

**Related ADR:** `CAT-ARCH-P3-59-ADR`; create or update the ADR whenever authority, trust, data, autonomy, provider, SLO, or deployment changes.

**Related documents:** `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the owning context, contract definitions, and recovery runbooks.

**AI context window:** The context manifest MUST include source hierarchy, authoritative facts, invariants, allowed tools, policy profile, tenant, data classification, budget, deadline, output schema, and acceptance tests.

**Verification:** Unit, contract, architecture, dependency, runtime, communication, knowledge-flow, context-flow, security, duplicate, timeout, and recovery tests are required at the risk-appropriate level.

**Review questions:** What is authoritative? What is proposed? What crosses the trust boundary? Can it run twice? How is refusal represented? How does an operator stop it? What proves success?

**Non-compliance:** Stop implementation, record the missing evidence, assign an owner, and either add the control or approve a time-bounded exception with compensating controls.

### P3-EVIDENCE-107 — Distributed Intelligence

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

### P3-EVIDENCE-122 — Agent Runtime

**Architecture ID:** CAT-ARCH-P3-EVIDENCE-122
**Title:** Agent Runtime implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one agent runtime obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Title:** Learning implementation evidence card
**Purpose:** Make one learning obligation explicit for implementation and review.
**Primary audience:** Human engineers, AI coding agents, reviewers, operators, and security auditors.
**Reading order:** Identity, context, policy, interface, execution, evidence, failure, recovery, and evolution.

**Architecture decision record:** The subsystem MUST remain governed, typed, observable, replaceable, and bounded. A provider or model response cannot become domain authority without an explicit decision.

**Architecture rationale:** CAT must remain understandable while models, providers, teams, and deployment environments change. Explicit contracts reduce unsafe reconstruction by future coding agents.

**Business perspective:** The control protects trust, operating cost, delivery speed, and the ability to explain or reverse a high-impact action.

**Engineering perspective:** Keep policy in the owning module, use ports for effects, normalize provider errors, version schemas, and test both happy and hostile paths.

**AI perspective:** Treat model text, retrieved content, memory, plans, tool arguments, and peer-agent messages as untrusted data until validated and authorized.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.

**Scalability contract:** Partition by tenant or capability where appropriate, apply backpressure, avoid unbounded context and memory, and scale stateless workers independently from authoritative stores.

**Future evolution:** Preserve stable identifiers, event schemas, provenance, policy authority, and migration paths through 2026, 2030, and 2035; replace models and adapters behind contracts.

**AI coding notes:** Read the AI workspace, numbered context documents, this section, ADRs, interfaces, tests, and runbooks. Make the smallest patch; do not infer missing permissions or silently expand the tool set.

**Implementation contract:** Use the approved language and runtime, typed interfaces, schema validation, idempotency, deadlines, cancellation, structured telemetry, safe migrations, and rollback or forward-fix evidence.

**Repository location:** Domain policy belongs in the owning bounded context; orchestration in the application layer; adapters in infrastructure; tests and schemas in approved paths; no hidden shared table access.

**Owner:** Named capability owner, with Architecture, Security, Platform, Data, SRE, and Product consulted according to risk.

**Related services:** Only declared context services, governance, identity, event, storage, retrieval, and provider ports; no ambient service discovery or undocumented network call.

**Related rules:** `context/02_PROJECT_RULES.md`, `context/03_TECH_STACK.md`, `.ai/RULES.md`, `.ai/AI_WORKFLOW.md`, and relevant security, coding, deployment, and directory rules.

**Related ADR:** `CAT-ARCH-P3-57-ADR`; create or update the ADR whenever authority, trust, data, autonomy, provider, SLO, or deployment changes.

**Related documents:** `context/00_PROJECT_CONTEXT.md`, `context/01_PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md`, `context/04_ARCHITECTURE.md`, the owning context, contract definitions, and recovery runbooks.

**AI context window:** The context manifest MUST include source hierarchy, authoritative facts, invariants, allowed tools, policy profile, tenant, data classification, budget, deadline, output schema, and acceptance tests.

**Verification:** Unit, contract, architecture, dependency, runtime, communication, knowledge-flow, context-flow, security, duplicate, timeout, and recovery tests are required at the risk-appropriate level.

**Review questions:** What is authoritative? What is proposed? What crosses the trust boundary? Can it run twice? How is refusal represented? How does an operator stop it? What proves success?

**Non-compliance:** Stop implementation, record the missing evidence, assign an owner, and either add the control or approve a time-bounded exception with compensating controls.

**Runtime perspective:** Carry principal, tenant, correlation, causation, policy version, budget, deadline, schema version, and provenance through every handoff.

**Failure architecture:** Reject malformed input; deny missing authorization; bound retries; quarantine poison messages; isolate provider failures; prevent duplicate effects; and expose terminal outcomes.

**Recovery architecture:** Preserve evidence sufficient for replay, compensation, reconciliation, deletion, and operator diagnosis. Verify recovery with a drill, not only a document.

**Security contract:** Enforce least privilege, data classification, tenant isolation, prompt-injection resistance, secret redaction, approval thresholds, and auditability.

**Performance contract:** Define latency class, throughput, concurrency, context size, model-token budget, storage growth, provider rate limits, and cost ceiling. Measure end to end.
